action: Current and former RPS students and staff: accept the free identity monitoring, complete the password reset, and do not reuse your old RPS password anywhere else.
exec: A weeks-long K-12 recovery with likely data exposure; the board is weighing a request for state cyber preparedness grants.
impact: More than 50 sites, over 22,000 students and over 4,000 staff were affected; a permanent network is being rebuilt from backups.
plain: A cyberattack knocked a Virginia school district of 22,000 students offline. Weeks later it is still rebuilding and says stolen data may be online.
summary: The Virginia school division said a cyberattack that began in October took the whole division offline, hitting classroom tools, phones and email, and still affects daily operations. Leaders said data accessed in the incident may have been posted on the dark web. A temporary network and Chromebooks on a separate server are in use, a division-wide password reset is underway and identity monitoring was extended to former students and staff.
title: Richmond Public Schools: forensic audit underway, data may be on dark web after October cyberattack

validation.note: Local TV station reporting officials' statements at a school board meeting.

review.note: Compared with WWBT report (Nov 11): October attack, division offline, forensic audit, possible dark-web posting, temporary network, password reset, 50 sites/22,000 students/4,000 staff, ID monitoring for former students and staff. Note: dated Nov 11, at the edge of the map window.
